name: How to Frame a Window Opening Properly

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Framing a new window opening can feel like a big project, but with the right steps, you can get it done right. First off, you absolutely need to get the manufacturer’s required rough opening dimensions. This isn't just about the window's size; it's the exact measurement the manufacturer specifies for the hole in your wall. Don't skip this! Once you have those precise numbers, you'll start framing the opening. This involves carefully installing king studs, which are the full-height studs on either side of the opening, and then adding jack studs, which support the header. The header is super important as it carries the load from above the window. Below the window, you'll put in a sill (or rough sill) and then cripples, which run from the sill down to the bottom plate. After you've got all those pieces in, it's time for some crucial checks. You need to make sure the opening is perfectly square, plumb (vertically straight), and level (horizontally flat). A great trick is to measure the diagonals of the opening—if they're equal, it's square! If not, you'll need to make adjustments before you move on to sheathing and flashing. Sometimes, especially if you're dealing with a load-bearing wall or you're unsure about header sizing or local building codes, bringing in a professional like HH Remodeling LLC can save you a lot of headaches.
